title: GCU vs NAU: control, tuition, size
summary: Grand Canyon University (GCU) versus Northern Arizona University (NAU). Also searched as NAU vs GCU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Northern Arizona University (NAU) and Grand Canyon University (GCU) differ primarily in ownership, enrollment, tuition, and location. NAU is a public institution located in Flagstaff, while GCU is a private nonprofit university based in Phoenix. The undergraduate enrollment at NAU is approximately 22,903 students, whereas GCU has a significantly larger undergraduate population of about 73,371. Tuition for in-state students at NAU is $13,009, which is lower compared to GCU's in-state tuition of $17,850. These distinctions highlight key differences between NAU vs GCU in terms of institutional type, size, cost, and geographic setting.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance between Northern Arizona University (NAU) and Grand Canyon University (GCU), there are notable differences in tuition and student debt. NAU's in-state tuition is $13,009, which is lower than GCU's in-state tuition of $17,850. For out-of-state students, NAU charges $29,881, whereas GCU's out-of-state tuition remains at $17,850. Regarding median debt upon program completion, NAU graduates carry a median debt of $19,000, while GCU graduates have a higher median debt of $22,114. These figures illustrate the financial considerations prospective students might evaluate when comparing NAU vs GCU.
